sentences.zh: ○李抱玉　李抱真　王虔休　盧從史　李芃李澄 族弟元素李抱玉李抱玉，武德功臣安興貴之裔。

translations.literal: ○ Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng, and his clansman Yuan Su — Li Baoyu. Li Baoyu was a descendant of An Xinggui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: [Section] Li Baoyu; Li Baozhen; Wang Qianxiu; Lu Congshi; Li Peng; Li Cheng and his clansman Yuan Su — Li Baoyu. Li Baoyu was descended from An Xinggui, a founding minister of the Wude reign.

sentences.zh: 代居河西，善養名馬，為時所稱。

translations.literal: For generations they lived in Hexi, skilled at raising famous horses, and were praised by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Hexi for generations and was famed for breeding excellent horses.

sentences.zh: 群從兄弟，或徙居京華，習文儒，與士人通婚者，稍染士風。

translations.literal: Among the cousins and brothers, some moved to the capital, studied letters and Confucian learning, and intermarried with scholars — gradually taking on the air of cultivated gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his kinsmen had relocated to the capital, taken up literary study, and married into scholar families, acquiring a touch of genteel culture.

sentences.zh: 抱玉少長西州，好騎射，常從軍幕，沉毅有謀，小心忠謹。

translations.literal: Baoyu grew up young in Xizhou, loved horseback riding and archery, often followed military headquarters, was steady and resolute with stratagems, and was careful, loyal, and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu had been raised in Xizhou from youth. He was fond of riding and archery, served regularly on campaign staffs, and was known for calm resolve, shrewd counsel, and scrupulous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，太尉李光弼引為偏裨，屢建勳績，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, Grand Preceptor Li Guangbi brought him in as a junior commander; he repeatedly achieved merit and thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyuan era (758–759), Li Guangbi, Grand Preceptor, took him on as a subordinate officer. His repeated battlefield successes soon made his name known.

sentences.zh: 二年，自特進、右羽林軍大將軍、知軍事，遷鴻臚卿員外置同正員，持節鄭州諸軍事兼鄭州刺史、攝御史中丞、鄭陳潁亳四州節度。

translations.literal: In the second year, from Extraordinary Grand Censor, Grand General of the Right Forest Army with knowledge of military affairs, he was promoted to Acting Commissioner-in-chief of the Court for Diplomatic Relations with the concurrent authority of a regular commissioner, holding credentials as military commissioner of Zhengzhou with concurrent post as Vice Censor-in-chief, and as military governor of the four prefectures Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he rose from extraordinary grand censor and commanding general of the Right Imperial Guard to provisional chief minister of state ceremonials with full commissioner's standing, with overall military command at Zhengzhou as vice censor-in-chief and as regional commander over Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 時史思明陷洛陽，光弼守河陽，賊兵鋒方盛，光弼謂抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Shi Siming had taken Luoyang; Guangbi was holding Heyang, and the rebel army's momentum was at its height. Guangbi said to Baoyu, "General, can you hold the southern city for me for two days?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming had seized Luoyang, and Guangbi was defending Heyang while rebel strength was at its peak. Guangbi asked Baoyu, "Can you hold the southern city for me for two days?

sentences.zh: 抱玉曰：「過期若何？」

translations.literal: Baoyu said, "What if the deadline passes?"
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu asked, "What if the two days pass?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「過期而救不至，任棄城也。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "If the deadline passes and relief does not arrive, you may abandon the city as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied, "If relief has not come by then, you are free to abandon the city."

sentences.zh: 賊帥周摯領安太清、徐黃玉等先次南城，將陷之，抱玉乃紿之曰：「吾糧盡，明日當降。」

translations.literal: The rebel commander Zhou Zhi, leading An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, first encamped at the southern city and was about to take it. Baoyu then deceived them, saying, "My grain is exhausted; tomorrow I shall surrender."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commander Zhou Zhi, with An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, had moved first against the southern city and was on the verge of taking it. Baoyu deceived them, saying, "Our provisions are gone; we will surrender tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 賊眾大喜，斂軍以俟之。

translations.literal: The rebel troops were greatly pleased and drew in their army to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were delighted and held their forces back to await the surrender.

sentences.zh: 抱玉因得繕完設備，明日，堅壁請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu thereby gained time to repair and complete his defenses. The next day he shut the walls tight and offered battle.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu used the delay to repair his defenses and stock supplies. The next day he shut the gates and challenged them to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊怒欺紿，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels, enraged at being deceived, pressed the attack urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at the deception, the rebels launched a fierce assault.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵，表裡夾攻，殺傷甚眾，摯軍退。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent out surprise troops and attacked from inside and outside at once, killing and wounding a great many; Zhi's army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent out ambush forces and struck from both sides, inflicting heavy casualties, and Zhou Zhi's army retreated.

sentences.zh: 光弼自將於中潬城，摯舍南城攻中潬，不勝，乃整軍將攻北城。

translations.literal: Guangbi himself commanded at Zhongtan city. Zhi abandoned the southern city and attacked Zhongtan but did not prevail; he then marshaled his army to attack the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi commanded in person at Zhongtan. Zhou Zhi left the southern city and assaulted Zhongtan without success, then regrouped to attack the northern city.

sentences.zh: 光弼以兵出戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Guangbi led his troops out to battle and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi met them in the field and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 固河陽，復懷州，皆功居第一，遷澤州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In securing Heyang and recovering Huaizhou, his merit ranked first; he was promoted to prefect of Zezhou and concurrent Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in merit for holding Heyang and recovering Huaizhou, and was appointed prefect of Ze and vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，擢為澤潞節度使、潞州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫，加領陳、鄭二州，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Baoyu was promoted to military governor of Zelu, chief administrator of the Lu prefecture metropolitan commandery, and concurrent Censor-in-chief, with added jurisdiction over Chen and Zheng prefectures, and was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong succeeded to the throne, Baoyu was made military governor of Zelu, chief administrator of Lu prefecture, and censor-in-chief, with added authority over Chen and Zheng, and was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 抱玉上言：「臣貫屬涼州，本姓安氏，以祿山構禍，恥與同姓，去至德二年五月，蒙恩賜姓李氏，今請割貫屬京兆府長安縣。」

translations.literal: Baoyu submitted a memorial: "Your servant's registered domicile is Liangzhou; my original surname was An. Because Lushan brought calamity, I was ashamed to share that surname. In the fifth month of the second year of Zhide I received the grace of being granted the surname Li. I now request that my registered domicile be transferred to Chang'an county in Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu memorialized the throne: "I am registered in Liangzhou and was born An. After Lushan's rebellion I was ashamed to bear that name; in May 757 I was honored with the imperial surname Li. I now ask that my registration be transferred to Chang'an county in the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 許之，因是舉宗並賜國姓。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and thereby the whole clan was granted the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and his entire clan received the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年冬，吐蕃寇京師，乘輿幸陝，諸軍潰卒及村閭亡命相聚為盜，京城南面子午等五穀群盜頗害居人，朝廷遣薛景仙領兵為五穀使招討，連月不捷，乃詔抱玉兼鳳翔節度使討之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangde, Tibetans raided the capital; the imperial carriage went to Shan. Routed soldiers of various armies and fugitives from villages gathered as bandits. In the southern suburbs of the capital, the bandits of the Five Valleys including Ziwu greatly harmed the inhabitants. The court sent Xue Jingxian to lead troops as commissioner for the Five Valleys to suppress them; for months he had no success. An edict then appointed Baoyu concurrently military governor of Fengxiang to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 763 Tibetans raided the capital and the emperor withdrew to Shan. Routed troops and village fugitives banded together as robbers, and the Five Valleys gangs south of the capital, including Ziwu, preyed heavily on the populace. Xue Jingxian was sent as Five Valleys commissioner to suppress them but met no success for months; Baoyu was then ordered to take concurrent command of Fengxiang and destroy the bandits.

sentences.zh: 抱玉探知賊帥行止之處，先分屯諸谷，乃設奇潛使輕銳數百南自洋州入攻之。

translations.literal: Baoyu investigated where the bandit chiefs were moving, first stationed detachments in the various valleys, then set an ambush and secretly sent several hundred light elite troops south from Yangzhou to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu learned where the bandit leaders were operating, posted troops in the valleys, then sent several hundred picked light troops in a surprise strike south from Yang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高玉方與諸偷會，遽為銳卒數十人掩擒之，因大搜獲偷黨，悉斬之，餘黨不討自潰，旬日內五穀平。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gao Yu was just meeting with the various thieves when suddenly several dozen elite troops seized him by surprise. A great search then captured the thief bands; all were beheaded. The remaining bands dispersed without further campaigning, and within ten days the Five Valleys were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chief Gao Yu was meeting with his fellows when several dozen elite soldiers seized him by surprise. A sweep captured the rest of the gang, who were all executed; the remnants melted away without further fighting, and the Five Valleys were pacified within ten days.

sentences.zh: 以功遷司空，余並如故。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to Minister of Works; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Minister of Works; his other offices were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃每歲犯境，上以岐陽國之西門，寄在抱玉，恩寵無比，遷同中書門下平章事，又兼山南西道節度使、河西隴右山南西道副元帥、判梁州事，連統三道節制，兼領鳳翔、潞、梁三大府，秩處三公。

translations.literal: At that time Tibetans raided the borders every year. The emperor regarded Qiyang as the western gate of the realm and entrusted it to Baoyu with incomparable favor. He was promoted to Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and concurrently military governor of Shannan West circuit, deputy commander-in-chief of Hexi, Longyou, and Shannan West, and administrator of Liangzhou — commanding three circuits in succession, and concurrently heading the three great prefectures Fengxiang, Lu, and Liang, with rank equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided the frontier yearly, and the emperor treated Qiyang as the realm's western gate and placed it in Baoyu's hands with unmatched favor. He rose to grand councilor, became military governor of Shannan West, deputy commander-in-chief over Hexi, Longyou, and Shannan West, and administrator of Liang — commanding three circuits and heading Fengxiang, Lu, and Liang, with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 抱玉以任位崇重，抗疏懇讓司空及山南西道節度、判梁州事，乞退授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baoyu, because his duties and rank were exalted, submitted a forthright memorial earnestly declining the post of Minister of Works and the posts of military governor of Shannan West and administrator of Liangzhou, requesting instead to step back to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his responsibilities too weighty, Baoyu petitioned earnestly to relinquish the Ministry of Works, the Shannan West governorship, and the Liangzhou post, asking to return to the Ministry of War alone.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其謙讓，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his modesty and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his humility and agreed.

sentences.zh: 抱雲凡鎮鳳翔十餘年，雖無破虜之功，而禁暴安人，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Baoyu in all governed Fengxiang for more than ten years; though he had no merit in defeating foreign enemies, in suppressing violence and settling the people he was quite praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu governed Fengxiang for more than ten years in all. He won no great victories over invaders, but his suppression of violence and protection of the people won wide contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 大曆十二年卒，上甚悼之，輟朝三日，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dali he died. The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 777. The emperor grieved deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 李抱真李抱真，抱玉從父弟也。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen — Baozhen was Baoyu's younger cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen was Baoyu's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 抱玉為澤潞節度使，甚器抱真，任以軍事，累授汾州別駕。

translations.literal: When Baoyu was military governor of Zelu, he greatly valued Baozhen and entrusted him with military affairs, repeatedly appointing him vice-prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyu was governor of Zelu he held Baozhen in high regard, entrusted him with military affairs, and repeatedly appointed him vice-prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 當是時，僕固懷恩反於汾州，抱真陷焉，乃脫身歸京師。

translations.literal: At that time Pugu Huai'en rebelled at Fenzhou and Baozhen was caught in it; he escaped and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled at Fen, Baozhen was trapped there but made his way back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗以懷恩倚回紇，所將朔方兵又勁，憂甚，召見抱真問狀，因奏曰：「郭子儀領朔方之眾，人多思之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong, because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and the Shuofang troops he led were also powerful, was deeply worried. He summoned Baozhen and questioned him about the situation. Baozhen thereupon memorialized: "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang forces; the men still long for him.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, deeply worried that Huai'en had Uyghur support and commanded the formidable Shuofang army, summoned Baozhen and questioned him. Baozhen replied, "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang troops, and the men still yearn for him.

sentences.zh: 懷恩欺其眾，曰『子儀為朝恩所殺』，詐而用之。

translations.literal: Huai'en deceived the troops, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by court favoritism,' and used them by fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en deceived them, claiming that Ziyi had been killed by court intrigue, and led them under false pretenses.

sentences.zh: 今復子儀之位，可不戰而克。」

translations.literal: If Ziyi's post is now restored, the enemy can be overcome without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Restore Ziyi to command, and they will collapse without a battle.

sentences.zh: 其後懷恩子瑒為其下所殺，懷恩奔遁，多如抱真策，因是遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: Afterward Huai'en's son Yang was killed by his subordinates, and Huai'en fled in flight — largely as Baozhen had strategized. For this he was promoted to Vice-Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huai'en's son Yang was killed by his own men and Huai'en fled — much as Baozhen had predicted. Baozhen was promoted to vice-director of the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，為陳鄭、澤潞節度留後，抱真因中謝言曰：「臣雖無可取，當今百姓勞逸，系在牧守，願得一郡以自試。」

translations.literal: Before long he served as acting military governor of Chen-Zheng and Zelu. At an audience of thanks Baozhen said, "Your servant, though without merit, knows that the people's toil and ease today depend on their prefects and governors. I wish to receive one prefecture to prove myself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became acting governor of Chen-Zheng and Zelu. At an audience of thanks Baozhen said, "I have little to offer, but the people's welfare depends on their local governors. I ask for a prefecture where I may prove myself.

sentences.zh: 上許之，改授澤州刺史，兼為澤潞節度副使。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it and transferred him to prefect of Zezhou, concurrently vice military governor of Zelu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed him prefect of Ze and vice governor of Zelu.

sentences.zh: 居二年，轉懷州刺史，復為懷澤潞觀察使留後，凡八年。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to prefect of Huaizhou, again serving as acting observation commissioner of Huai-Zelu, in all for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became prefect of Huai and again served as acting observation commissioner of Huai and Zelu — eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 抱玉卒，抱真仍領留後。

translations.literal: When Baoyu died, Baozhen continued as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyu died, Baozhen remained as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 抱真密揣山東當有變，上黨且當兵沖，是時乘戰余之地，土瘠賦重，人益困，無以養軍士。

translations.literal: Baozhen secretly judged that Shandong would soon see upheaval and that Shangdang would be a military choke point. At that time it was a land worn by war: the soil was poor, taxes heavy, and the people ever more distressed, with no means to support the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen privately concluded that Shandong would soon erupt in rebellion and that Shangdang would be a strategic battleground. The region was war-ravaged, the land poor and taxes heavy; the people grew poorer still and could not sustain the army.

sentences.zh: 籍戶丁男，三選其一，有材力者免其租徭，給弓矢，令之曰：「農之隙，則分曹角射；

translations.literal: He registered household adult males and chose one in three; those with strength and ability were exempted from rent and corvée, given bows and arrows, and ordered: "In the intervals of farming, divide into groups and compete in archery;
translations.idiomatic: He registered adult males and selected one in three; the able-bodied were exempted from rent and labor service and given bows. He ordered them, "In slack farming seasons, divide into squads and practice archery;

sentences.zh: 歲終，吾當會試。」

translations.literal: at year's end I shall hold a general examination.
translations.idiomatic: at year's end I will hold a general examination.

sentences.zh: 及期，按簿而征之，都試以示賞罰，覆命之如初。

translations.literal: When the time came, he summoned them according to the registers, held a collective examination to show reward and punishment, and sent them back to training as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came he summoned them by register, held a collective examination with rewards and penalties, and sent them back to drill as before.

sentences.zh: 比三年，則皆善射，抱真曰：「軍可用矣。」

translations.literal: After about three years, all were skilled archers. Baozhen said, "The army is ready for use.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they were all skilled archers. Baozhen said, "The army is ready.

sentences.zh: 於是舉部內鄉兵，得成卒二萬，前既不廩費，府庫益實，乃繕甲兵，為戰具，遂雄視山東。

translations.literal: He then raised militia throughout his jurisdiction and obtained twenty thousand trained soldiers. Because he had spent nothing from the granaries before, the treasury grew fuller; he then repaired armor and weapons and made war equipment, and came to dominate Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised militia throughout his circuit and fielded twenty thousand trained troops. Having spent nothing from the granaries, his treasury grew rich; he outfitted armor and weapons and came to dominate Shandong.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下稱昭義軍步兵冠諸軍。

translations.literal: At that time the realm acclaimed the infantry of the Zhaoyi army as foremost among all armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Zhaoyi infantry were considered the finest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 無幾，復代李承昭為昭義軍及磁邢節度觀察留後，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he again replaced Li Chengzhao as acting military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhaoyi army and Ci-Xing circuits, and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he succeeded Li Chengzhao as acting governor of the Zhaoyi army and the Ci-Xing circuits, with the additional title of regular attendant at the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，拜檢校工部尚書，兼潞州長史、昭義軍節度支度營田、澤潞磁邢觀察使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Baozhen was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrent chief administrator of Luzhou, commissioner for supplies, farming, and garrisons of the Zhaoyi army, and observation commissioner of Zelu, Ci, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded, Baozhen was made acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Lu, commissioner for Zhaoyi supplies and garrison farming, and observation commissioner over Zelu, Ci, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，田悅以魏博反，乃悉兵圍邢州及臨洺益急，詔河東節度使馬燧及神策兵救之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Tian Yue rebelled with Weibo and mustered all his troops to besiege Xingzhou and Linming with growing urgency. An edict ordered Ma Sui, military governor of Hedong, and the Shence troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In 781 Tian Yue rebelled with Weibo and pressed the siege of Xing and Linming. Ma Sui of Hedong and the Shence army were ordered to the relief.

sentences.zh: 抱真與燧敗悅兵於雙岡，斬悅將楊朝光，又擊破悅於臨洺，遂解臨洺及邢州之圍，以功加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baozhen and Sui defeated Yue's troops at Shuanggang, beheaded Yue's general Yang Chaoguang, and again defeated Yue at Linming, thereby lifting the sieges of Linming and Xingzhou. For this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen and Sui defeated Yue at Shuanggang, beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, and routed him again at Linming, lifting both sieges. Baozhen was made acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復與燧大破悅於洹水，悅以數百騎走歸魏州。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he inflicted a great defeat on Yue at Huanshui; Yue fled with several hundred horsemen back to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Sui he again crushed Yue at Huanshui, and Yue fled to Wei with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 復與燧圍魏州，又敗悅於城下，以功加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he besieged Weizhou and again defeated Yue below the walls. For this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: With Sui he besieged Wei and defeated Yue again beneath the walls, earning appointment as acting right vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時悅窘蹙，硃滔、王武俊皆反，聯兵救悅，抱真與燧等退次魏縣。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was hard pressed; Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun both rebelled and joined forces to rescue Yue. Baozhen and Sui and the others withdrew and encamped at Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was cornered when Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun also rebelled and marched to his relief. Baozhen, Sui, and the others fell back to Wei county.

sentences.zh: 上幸奉天，中使告問至，諸將皆仰天慟哭。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Fengtian; when the palace envoy arrived with inquiries, all the generals looked up to heaven and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Fengtian. When the palace envoy arrived with news, the generals looked heavenward and wept.

sentences.zh: 李懷光席捲奔命，馬燧、李芃各引兵歸鎮。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang swept off in haste to answer the summons; Ma Sui and Li Peng each led their troops back to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang rushed off to the emperor's aid; Ma Sui and Li Peng each withdrew to their own circuits.

sentences.zh: 硃泚既汙宮闕，時李希烈陷大梁，李納亦反鄆州。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had already defiled the palace; at that time Li Xilie had taken Daliang, and Li Na also rebelled at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had seized the capital; Li Xilie held Daliang, and Li Na rebelled at Yan.

sentences.zh: 無何，上幸梁州，李懷光又竊據河中。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor went to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang again seized Hedong by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang seized Hedong as well.

sentences.zh: 抱真獨於擾攘傾潰之中，以山東三州外抗群賊，內輯軍士，群賊深憚之。

translations.literal: Baozhen alone amid turmoil and collapse, with three Shandong prefectures, resisted the rebel hosts outwardly and kept his soldiers in order inwardly; the rebel hosts deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Amid universal turmoil Baozhen alone, holding three Shandong prefectures, held the rebels at bay without and kept discipline within; the rebel hosts feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 興元初，遷檢校左僕射、平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was promoted to Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Left and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In early 784 he was made acting left vice director of the imperial secretariat and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時硃滔悉幽薊軍，借兵回紇，擁眾五萬，南向以應泚，攻圍貝州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao mustered the armies of You and Ji, borrowed Uyghur troops, and with a host of fifty thousand marched south to support Ci, besieging Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao then mobilized the You-Ji armies, borrowed Uyghur troops, and with fifty thousand men marched south to support Ci, besieging Bei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，群賊附於希烈，希烈僭偽，有臣屬群賊意，群心稍離。

translations.literal: At first the rebel hosts had attached themselves to Xilie; Xilie had usurped the throne and intended to make the rebel hosts his subjects, and their hearts gradually turned away.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hosts had initially rallied to Li Xilie, but when he declared himself emperor and sought to subordinate them, their loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 上自奉天下罪己之詔，悉赦群賊，抱真乃遣門客賈林以大義說武俊，合從擊硃滔，武俊許之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued from Fengtian an edict blaming himself and pardoning all the rebel hosts. Baozhen then sent his client Jia Lin to persuade Wujun with the great principle of righteousness to join in attacking Zhu Tao; Wujun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued from Fengtian a self-reproach edict pardoning all rebels. Baozhen sent his retainer Jia Lin to persuade Wang Wujun in the name of righteousness to join against Zhu Tao, and Wujun agreed.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍尚相疑，抱真乃以數騎徑入武俊營。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies still mistrusted each other; Baozhen therefore rode with only a few horsemen straight into Wujun's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies still distrusted each other, so Baozhen rode into Wujun's camp with only a handful of men.

sentences.zh: 其將去也，賓客皆止之，抱真遣軍司馬盧玄卿勒軍部分曰：「僕今日此舉，系天下安危。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, his guests all tried to stop him. Baozhen sent his army marshal Lu Xuanqing to address the troops in formation: "Your servant's act today concerns the safety of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His staff tried to dissuade him, but Baozhen sent his army marshal Lu Xuanqing to address the troops: "What I do today concerns the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 僕死不還，領軍事以聽朝命，亦唯子；

translations.literal: If your servant dies and does not return, take command of military affairs and obey court orders — that too is yours alone;
translations.idiomatic: If I do not return, take command and obey the court — that duty falls to you alone;

sentences.zh: 奮勵士馬，東向雪僕之恥，亦唯子。」

translations.literal: rouse the soldiers and horses, march east to wipe away your servant's shame — that too is yours alone.
translations.idiomatic: and if you must rouse the army and march east to avenge my death, that too is yours alone.

sentences.zh: 言訖而去。

translations.literal: Having spoken, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he rode off.

sentences.zh: 武俊設備甚嚴，抱真曰：「硃泚、希烈僭竊大位，硃滔攻圍貝州，此輩皆欲陵駕吾屬。

translations.literal: Wujun had made his guard very strict. Baozhen said, "Zhu Ci and Xilie have usurped the throne; Zhu Tao is besieging Beizhou — these men all wish to ride over us.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun had posted strict guards. Baozhen said, "Zhu Ci and Xilie have usurped the throne, and Zhu Tao is besieging Bei — they mean to dominate us all.

sentences.zh: 足下既不能自振數賊之上，舍九葉天子而北面臣反虜乎？

translations.literal: If you, sir, cannot raise yourself above these several rebels, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and face north to serve as subject to a rebel usurper?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot stand above these rebels, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and bow north to a usurper?

sentences.zh: 乃者聖上奉天下罪己之詔，可謂禹、湯之主也。」

translations.literal: Just now the sage emperor has issued an edict blaming himself before the realm — he may be called a ruler like Yu or Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has just issued a self-reproach edict to the realm — he is a ruler in the mold of Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 因言及播越，持武俊哭，涕泗交下，武俊亦哭，感動左右。

translations.literal: He then spoke of the emperor's exile, took hold of Wujun and wept; tears streamed down both their faces. Wujun also wept, moving those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of the emperor's exile, seized Wujun's hands, and wept until both men were in tears, moving everyone present.

sentences.zh: 因退臥武俊帳中，酣寢久之。

translations.literal: He then withdrew and lay down in Wujun's tent, sleeping soundly for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired to Wujun's tent and slept soundly for a long time.

sentences.zh: 武俊感其不疑，待之益恭，指心仰天曰：「此身已許公死敵矣。」

translations.literal: Wujun, moved by his lack of suspicion, treated him with still greater respect, pointed to his heart and looked up to heaven, saying, "This body is already pledged to you, sir, to die against your enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by such trust, Wujun treated him with still greater respect, laid his hand on his heart, and swore to heaven, "This life is yours — I will die at your side against your enemies.

sentences.zh: 遂與結為兄弟而別，約明日合戰，遂擊破硃滔於經城，以功加檢校司空，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: They then swore brotherhood and parted, agreeing to join battle the next day. They thereupon defeated Zhu Tao at Jingcheng. For this merit Baozhen was given the additional post of Acting Minister of Works and a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: They swore brotherhood and parted, agreeing to fight together the next day. They then routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng. Baozhen was made acting Minister of Works with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，朝於京師，居頃之，還鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he attended court in the capital; after a short stay he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he visited the capital, and after a brief stay returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 抱真沉斷多智計，嘗欲招致天下賢俊，聞人之善，必令持貨幣數千里邀致之；

translations.literal: Baozhen was deep, decisive, and full of stratagems. He once wished to gather worthy men from across the realm; when he heard of someone's excellence, he always sent men with gifts for thousands of li to invite them;
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was shrewd, resolute, and resourceful. He sought to gather talented men from across the empire; whenever he heard of someone's merit he sent envoys with gifts thousands of li to invite them;

sentences.zh: 至與語無可採者，漸退之。

translations.literal: when after conversation there was nothing worth taking from them, he gradually sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: but if conversation revealed nothing worthwhile, he quietly let them go.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，乃大起台榭，穿池沼以自娛。

translations.literal: When the realm was at peace he greatly raised terraces and pavilions and dug ponds for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire was at peace he built grand pavilions and dug ornamental ponds for his amusement.

sentences.zh: 晚節又好方士，以冀長生。

translations.literal: In his later years he also favored alchemical masters, hoping for long life.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he also turned to Daoist alchemists, hoping for immortality.

sentences.zh: 有孫季長者，為抱真練金丹，紿抱真曰：「服之當升仙」遂署為賓僚。

translations.literal: There was one Sun Jichang who refined golden elixirs for Baozhen and deceived him, saying, "If you take this you will ascend as an immortal." He was then appointed to his staff of guests and officials.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixirs for him and promised, "Take this and you will ascend as an immortal." Baozhen appointed him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 數謂參佐曰：「此丹秦皇、漢武皆不能得，唯我遇之，他年朝上清，不復偶公輩矣。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly told his aides: "This elixir neither the First Emperor of Qin nor Emperor Wu of Han could obtain; only I have encountered it. In years to come I shall ascend to the Upper Clarity and will no longer keep company with you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He told his staff repeatedly, "Neither the First Emperor nor Han Wudi could obtain this elixir — only I have. One day I will ascend to heaven and leave your company behind.

sentences.zh: 復夢駕鶴衝天，寤而刻木鶴、衣道士衣以習乘之。

translations.literal: He also dreamed of riding a crane soaring to heaven; on waking he carved a wooden crane, put on a Daoist priest's robe, and practiced riding it.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of riding a crane to heaven; on waking he carved a wooden crane, donned Daoist robes, and practiced mounting it.

sentences.zh: 凡服丹二萬丸，腹堅不食，將死，不知人者數日矣。

translations.literal: In all he took twenty thousand pills; his belly became hard and he ate nothing. As death approached, he did not recognize people for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed twenty thousand pills until his belly hardened and he could not eat. For days before death he did not recognize anyone.

sentences.zh: 道士牛洞玄以豬肪谷漆下之，殆盡。

translations.literal: The Daoist Niu Dongxuan used lard, grain, and lacquer to purge him — nearly to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Niu Dongxuan purged him with lard, grain porridge, and lacquer — nearly killing him in the process.

sentences.zh: 病少間，季長復曰：「垂上仙，何自棄也！」

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, Jichang again said, "You are on the verge of becoming a transcendent — why abandon it yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When he briefly recovered, Jichang urged, "You are on the verge of transcendence — why give up now!

sentences.zh: 益服三千丸，頃之卒。

translations.literal: He took three thousand more pills and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He took three thousand more pills and soon died.

sentences.zh: 初，抱真久疾，好禨祥，或令厭勝，為巫祝所惑，請降官爵以禳除之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Baozhen had long been ill and favored omens and portents; sometimes he ordered exorcistic rites and was deluded by shamans and prayer-masters, requesting to lower his rank and titles to avert calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen had long been ill and obsessed with omens and exorcism, deluded by shamans into petitioning to lower his rank to ward off misfortune.

sentences.zh: 是年，凡七上章讓司空，復為檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: That year he submitted seven memorials declining the Ministry of Works and was again Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: That year he submitted seven petitions declining the Ministry of Works and was restored to acting left vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年卒，時年六十二，廢朝三日，贈太保，賻以布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, and funeral gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were given in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 794 at sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 抱真薨之日，其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪不發。

translations.literal: On the day Baozhen died, his son, Palace Attendant-in-ordinary Jian, concealed the death and did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Baozhen died his son Jian, a palace attendant, concealed the death and did not announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 營田副使盧會昌令抱真從甥元仲經潛與緘謀，其明日，將吏會集，仲經詐為抱真令曰：「吾疾甚，不能蒞職，今令緘掌軍事，諸軍善佐之。」

translations.literal: The vice commissioner for garrison farming Lu Huichang had Baozhen's cousin Yuan Zhongjing secretly plot with Jian. The next day, when officers assembled, Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "I am gravely ill and cannot attend to duty. I now appoint Jian to command military affairs; all armies, support him well.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner for garrison farming Lu Huichang had Baozhen's cousin Yuan Zhongjing plot secretly with Jian. The next day, when officers assembled, Zhongjing forged an order: "I am gravely ill and cannot command. Jian will take military affairs; support him well.

sentences.zh: 節度副使李說及諸將吏俯首，皆曰：「諾」。

translations.literal: The vice military governor Li Shuo and all the generals and officers bowed their heads and all said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Vice governor Li Shuo and the other officers bowed and assented.

sentences.zh: 須臾，緘盛服而出，眾皆拜之，緘乃悉府藏頒賞軍士。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Jian came out in full dress; all bowed to him. Jian then distributed the entire treasury to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Jian appeared in full regalia; all bowed to him, and he distributed the entire treasury to the troops.

sentences.zh: 盧會昌仍詐為抱真表，請以職事付緘。

translations.literal: Lu Huichang again forged a memorial in Baozhen's name requesting that official duties be entrusted to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huichang forged a memorial in Baozhen's name asking that command be transferred to Jian.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又令諸將連奏請緘領軍。

translations.literal: The next day he again had the generals submit joint memorials requesting that Jian lead the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he had the generals submit joint petitions asking that Jian take command.

sentences.zh: 上已聞真疾病，請見明日。

translations.literal: The emperor had already heard that Baozhen was ill and requested an audience the next day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already heard Baozhen was ill and asked to see him the next day.

sentences.zh: 如此者凡三日，緘乃出造中使，左右皆陳兵，甚嚴備。

translations.literal: This went on for three days in all; then Jian came out to meet the palace envoy, with troops deployed on either side in very strict array.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for three days; then Jian came out to meet the palace envoy, flanked by heavily armed troops.

sentences.zh: 中使謂緘曰：「朝廷已知相公薨歿，令以兵務屬延貴，侍御宜歸發喪行服也。」

translations.literal: The envoy said to Jian, "The court already knows that the lord has died. It orders that military affairs be given to Yanguì. Attendant, you should return home to announce the mourning and observe the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy told Jian, "The court knows your father is dead. Military affairs are assigned to Yanguì. You should go home and observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 緘愕然，出謂諸將曰：「有詔不許緘掌事，諸公意若何？」

translations.literal: Jian was startled. He went out and said to the generals, "There is an edict forbidding Jian to hold command — what do you gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian was stunned. He went out and asked the generals, "The edict forbids me to command — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 將吏莫有對者。

translations.literal: None of the generals and officers had any reply.
translations.idiomatic: No officer spoke up.

sentences.zh: 緘懼而退，遽以使印及管鑰歸監軍。

translations.literal: Jian, in fear, withdrew and hastily returned the envoy's seal and the keys of office to the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Jian withdrew and hastily returned the command seal and keys to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 是日，乃發喪，畢一哭。

translations.literal: That same day he announced the mourning and completed the first wailing.
translations.idiomatic: That day he announced the death and performed the first mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 中使召延貴，以口詔令視事，趣遣緘赴東都。

translations.literal: The palace envoy summoned Yanguì and, by oral edict, ordered him to take up duties, urging that Jian be sent to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy summoned Yanguì, ordered him by oral edict to assume command, and directed Jian to proceed to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 元仲經逃於外，延貴捕得殺之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongjing fled abroad; Yanguì captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongjing had fled; Yanguì captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 既歸罪仲經，盧會昌得不坐。

translations.literal: Once guilt was laid on Zhongjing, Lu Huichang was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: With blame placed on Zhongjing, Lu Huichang escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 緘初謀亂，遣裨將陳榮詐以文書告成德節度使王武俊，求假財帛，武俊大怒曰：「吾與汝府公善者，冀恭王命，非同惡也。

translations.literal: When Jian first plotted rebellion, he sent his lieutenant Chen Rong with a forged document to inform Wang Wujun, military governor of Chengde, requesting borrowed funds and goods. Wujun was greatly angered and said, "I was on good terms with your father's lord, hoping to honor the king's command together — not to share in evil together.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian first plotted his coup, he sent lieutenant Chen Rong with a forged letter to Wang Wujun of Chengde asking for money and supplies. Wujun was furious: "Your father and I were allies in honoring the throne — not partners in treason.

sentences.zh: 今聞已亡，孰詐令其子而不俟朝旨耶？

translations.literal: Now I hear he is dead — who would deceive his son into acting without awaiting court orders?
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear he is dead — who would trick his son into seizing power without waiting for the court?

sentences.zh: 何敢告我，況有求也！」

translations.literal: How dare he inform me — and moreover make a request!
translations.idiomatic: How dare he come to me — and ask for favors besides!

sentences.zh: 乃囚陳榮而遣使讓緘焉。

translations.literal: He then imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to rebuke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to rebuke Jian.

sentences.zh: 王虔休王虔休，字君佐，汝州梁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu — Wang Qianxiu, courtesy name Junzuo, was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu, courtesy name Junzuo, was a native of Liang in Ru prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名延貴。

translations.literal: His original name was Yanguì.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yanguì.

sentences.zh: 少涉獵書籍，鄉里間以信義畏慕之，尤好武藝。

translations.literal: In youth he dabbled in books; in his home district people respected and admired him for faith and righteousness, and he especially loved martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read widely; neighbors respected him for integrity and admired his martial skill.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，汝州刺史李深用之為將。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Li Shen, prefect of Ruzhou, employed him as a general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era Li Shen, prefect of Ru, employed him as an officer.

sentences.zh: 久之，澤潞節度李抱真聞名，厚以財帛招之，累授兵馬使押衙。

translations.literal: After a long while, Li Baozhen, military governor of Zelu, heard of his fame and recruited him generously with wealth and silks, repeatedly appointing him as commander of horse and foot troops and as guard officer of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Baozhen of Zelu heard of him and recruited him with generous gifts, appointing him repeatedly as headquarters guard officer and commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 建中初，抱真統兵馬與諸將征討河北，其雙岡、水寨營等陣，虔休攻戰居多，擢為步軍都虞候，累加兼御史中丞、大夫，賜實封百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Baozhen commanded horse and foot troops with the generals to campaign in Hebei; at the formations of Shuanggang, Shuizhai camp, and others, Qianxiu fought in the majority of assaults. He was promoted to chief adjutant of the infantry, repeatedly given the additional posts of Vice Censor-in-chief and Censor-in-chief, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Baozhen led campaigns in Hebei; Qianxiu fought in most of the major engagements at Shuanggang and Shuizhai. He was made chief adjutant of the infantry, promoted to vice and then full censor-in-chief, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 洎抱真卒，裨將元仲經等議立抱真子緘，軍中擾亂，虔休正色言於眾曰：「軍州是天子軍州，將帥闕，合待朝命，何乃云云，妄生異意！」

translations.literal: When Baozhen died, the lieutenants Yuan Zhongjing and others discussed installing Baozhen's son Jian. The army was in turmoil. Qianxiu said sternly to the assembly: "Army and prefecture belong to the Son of Heaven. When the commander is absent, we should await court orders — why all this talk and reckless stirring of dissent!
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen died, lieutenants including Yuan Zhongjing plotted to install his son Jian, throwing the army into turmoil. Qianxiu addressed the troops sternly: "This command belongs to the Son of Heaven. With no commander, we must await court orders — why breed sedition?

sentences.zh: 軍中服從其言，由是竟免潰亂。

translations.literal: The army submitted to his words, and thereby was finally spared collapse and riot.
translations.idiomatic: The troops accepted his words, and the command was spared a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知而嘉之，以邕王為昭義節度觀察大使，授虔休潞州左司馬，依前兼御史大夫，掌留後，仍賜名虔休。

translations.literal: The court learned of this and commended him. The Prince of Yong was made grand observation commissioner of the Zhaoyi army; Qianxiu was appointed Left Administrator of Lu prefecture, continuing as concurrent Censor-in-chief, holding acting governorship, and was moreover granted the name Qianxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of this and commended him. The Prince of Yong was made grand observation commissioner of Zhaoyi; Qianxiu was appointed left administrator of Lu, retained his post as censor-in-chief as acting governor, and was granted the name Qianxiu.

sentences.zh: 號令安撫。

translations.literal: His orders pacified and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: His orders restored calm.

sentences.zh: 軍州大理。

translations.literal: Army and prefecture were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Army and prefecture were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 二歲，遷潞州長史、昭義軍節度、澤潞磁邢洺觀察使，尋加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to chief administrator of Luzhou, military governor of the Zhaoyi army, and observation commissioner of Zelu, Ci, Xing, and Ming, and soon given the additional post of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became chief administrator of Lu, military governor of Zhaoyi, and observation commissioner over Zelu, Ci, Xing, and Ming, and soon was made acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 799 at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈左僕射，賻以布帛米粟。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously given the Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and funeral gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously made left vice director of the imperial secretariat, with gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain.

sentences.zh: 虔休性恭勤，儉省節用，管內州倉庾皆積糧儲，可支軍人數歲。

translations.literal: Qianxiu's nature was respectful and diligent; he was frugal and economical. In every prefectural granary within his jurisdiction grain was stored in reserve, enough to supply the army for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu was respectful, diligent, and frugal. Every granary in his circuit held reserves sufficient to feed the army for years.

sentences.zh: 又嘗撰《誕聖樂曲》以進，其表曰：

translations.literal: He also once composed the "Music for the Birth of the Sage" and presented it; his memorial said:
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Music for the Birth of the Sage" and presented it with a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 先時，有太常樂工劉玠流落至潞州，虔休因令造此曲以進，今《中和樂》起此也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices musician Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu therefore had him compose this piece to present. Today's "Central Harmony Music" originated from this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court musician Liu Jie had drifted to Lu; Qianxiu had him compose this piece for presentation. The present "Central Harmony Music" originated here.

sentences.zh: 盧從史盧從史，其先自元魏已來，冠冕頗盛。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi — Lu Congshi's forebears from the Northern Wei onward had been quite illustrious in official caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi — his family had held high office since the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父虔，少孤，好學，舉進士，歷御史府三院、刑部郎中、江汝二州刺史、秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Qian was orphaned young, loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served in the three bureaus of the Censorate, as Director in the Ministry of Justice, as prefect of the two prefectures Jiang and Ru, and as Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian was orphaned young, loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served in the censorate, as director in the Ministry of Justice, as prefect of Jiang and Ru, and as director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 從史少矜力，習騎射，游澤、潞間，節度使李長榮用為大將。

translations.literal: Congshi in youth prided himself on strength, studied riding and archery, wandered between Ze and Lu, and was employed as a great general by the military governor Li Changrong.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi prided himself on strength in youth, trained in riding and archery, and wandered between Ze and Lu until Li Changrong employed him as a senior general.

sentences.zh: 德宗中歲，每命節制，必令採訪本軍為其所歸者。

translations.literal: In Dezong's middle years, whenever a military governorship was appointed, he always ordered investigation of whom the native army would follow.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's middle years, whenever a governorship was filled, the court first investigated whom the local army would accept.

sentences.zh: 長榮卒，從史因軍情，且善迎奉中使，得授昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Changrong died, Congshi, relying on army sentiment and being skilled at welcoming and serving palace envoys, obtained appointment as military governor of the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: When Changrong died, Congshi won army support and courted palace envoys skillfully, and was appointed military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 漸狂恣不道，至奪部將妻妾，而辯給矯妄，從事孔戡等以言直不從引去。

translations.literal: He gradually became wildly unrestrained and lawless, even seizing the wives and concubines of his subordinate generals. He was eloquent but deceitful and arrogant; his staff member Kong Kan and others, because their straightforward words were not heeded, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He grew wildly lawless, even seizing his officers' wives. Eloquent but deceitful, he drove away staff such as Kong Kan when they spoke plainly and were ignored.

sentences.zh: 前年丁父憂，朝旨未議起復，屬王士真卒，從史竊獻誅承宗計，以希上意，用是起授，委其成功。

translations.literal: The year before last he entered mourning for his father; court opinion had not yet discussed recall from mourning. When Wang Shizhen died, Congshi secretly submitted a plan to execute Cheng Zong to win the emperor's favor; for this he was recalled and appointed, with success entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier he had entered mourning for his father and the court had not yet decided on recall. When Wang Shizhen died, Congshi secretly proposed killing Cheng Zong to please the emperor; he was recalled from mourning and entrusted with the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及詔下討賊，兵出，逗留不進，陰與承宗通謀，令軍士潛懷賊號，又高其芻粟之價，售於度支，諷朝廷求宰相；

translations.literal: When the edict to campaign against the rebels was issued and troops marched out, he lingered without advancing, secretly conspiring with Cheng Zong, ordering soldiers covertly to keep rebel battle cries, also raising the price of his fodder and grain and selling to the Commissariat, and insinuating to the court that he should be made chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign edict came he marched out but stalled, secretly conspiring with Cheng Zong, letting his men keep rebel slogans, inflating fodder prices sold to the commissariat, and hinting that he deserved a seat at court;

sentences.zh: 且誣奏諸軍與賊通，兵不可進。

translations.literal: and moreover falsely memorialized that the various armies were in communication with the rebels and that troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: and falsely reported that allied armies were colluding with the rebels so that no advance was possible.

sentences.zh: 上深患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 護軍中尉吐突承璀將神策兵與之對壘，從史往往過其營博戲。

translations.literal: The Protector Army Commandant Tuhu Chenghui led Shence troops to face him in camp; Congshi often came to his camp to gamble.
translations.idiomatic: Army protector Tuhu Chenghui led Shence troops against him; Congshi often visited his camp to gamble.

sentences.zh: 從史沓貪好得，承璀出寶帶、奇玩以炫燿之，時其愛悅而遺焉，從史喜甚，日益狎。

translations.literal: Congshi was greedy and covetous of gain. Chenghui produced jeweled belts and rare curios to dazzle him, and when Congshi showed delight would present them to him. Congshi was greatly pleased and grew daily more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi was greedy and acquisitive. Chenghui displayed jeweled belts and rare curios to dazzle him and gave them whenever Congshi showed delight; Congshi grew ever more intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 上知其事，取裴垍之謀，因戒承璀伺其來博，揖語，幕下伏壯士，突起，持捽出帳後縛之，內車中，馳以赴闕。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of this and adopted Pei Ji's plan, instructing Chenghui to watch for when Congshi came to gamble, exchange greetings, have stalwart men hidden below the tent curtain spring up, seize and drag him out behind the tent and bind him, put him inside a carriage, and gallop to present him at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted Pei Ji's plan: when Congshi came to gamble, Chenghui was to greet him while braves hidden in the tent seized him, bound him, loaded him into a carriage, and rushed him to court.

sentences.zh: 從者驚亂，斬十數人，余號令乃定，且宣諭密詔，追赴闕庭。

translations.literal: His attendants were startled into disorder; more than ten were beheaded before the rest were brought to order by command, and a secret edict was proclaimed announcing that he was being escorted to court.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants panicked; more than ten were killed before order was restored and a secret edict announced that he was being taken to court.

sentences.zh: 都將烏重胤素懷忠順，乃嚴戒其軍，眾不敢動。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Wu Chongyin had long harbored loyal submission; he strictly warned his army, and the troops did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wu Chongyin, who had long been loyal, strictly restrained his troops and prevented a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 會夜，使疾驅，未明出境，道路人莫知。

translations.literal: It happened to be night; they drove hard, and before dawn had left the border; travelers on the road knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They rode through the night and crossed the border before dawn; no one on the road knew.

sentences.zh: 元和五年四月，制曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuanhe, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 810 an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 子繼宗等四人並貶嶺外。

translations.literal: His sons Jizong and the other four men were all demoted beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jizong and three others were all banished beyond the Ling range.

sentences.zh: 李芃李芃，字茂初，趙郡人也。

translations.literal: Li Peng — Li Peng, courtesy name Maochu, was a native of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Peng, courtesy name Maochu, was a native of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 解褐上邽主簿，三遷試大理評事，攝監察御史、山南東道觀察支使。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office robes he was recorder of Shanggui, was thrice promoted to probationary appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and acted as Investigating Censor and supply commissioner of the Shannan East circuit observation mission.
translations.idiomatic: He began as recorder of Shanggui, rose thrice to probationary appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and served as investigating censor and supply commissioner for Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 嚴武為京兆尹，舉為長安尉。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he recommended Peng as bailiff of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu was metropolitan magistrate of the capital, he recommended Peng as bailiff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李勉為江西觀察使，署奏秘書郎、兼監察御史，為判官。

translations.literal: When Li Mian was observation commissioner of Jiangxi, he appointed and memorialized Peng as Secretary of the Palace Library and concurrent Investigating Censor, as his administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mian was observation commissioner of Jiangxi, he appointed Peng secretary of the palace library and concurrent investigating censor as his aide.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，轉兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he was transferred to concurrent Attendant Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongtai (765) he became concurrent palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時宣、饒二州人方清、陳莊聚眾據山洞，西絕江路，劫商旅以為亂。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuan and Rao prefectures gathered crowds and held mountain caves, cutting the western river route and robbing merchants and travelers to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuan and Rao gathered bandits in mountain caves, cut the western river route, and plundered merchants.

sentences.zh: 芃乃請於秋浦置州，守其要地，以破其謀。

translations.literal: Peng then requested establishing a prefecture at Qiupu to guard the strategic point and break their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Peng proposed establishing a prefecture at Qiupu to hold the strategic point and break their plans.

sentences.zh: 李勉然其計，以聞，代宗嘉之，以宣州之秋浦、青陽、饒州之至德置池州焉。

translations.literal: Li Mian approved his plan and reported it; Emperor Daizong commended it and established Chizhou from Qiupu and Qingyang of Xuanzhou and Zhide of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian approved and reported the plan; Daizong commended it and created Chi prefecture from Qiupu and Qingyang of Xuan and Zhide of Rao.

sentences.zh: 芃攝行事，無幾，乃兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Peng acted in administrative affairs; before long he was given the concurrent post of Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Peng administered the new prefecture and soon received the concurrent post of attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 居無何，魏少游代勉為使，復署奏檢校虞部員外郎，賜金紫，為都團練副使。

translations.literal: Before long Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian as commissioner; he again appointed and memorialized Peng as Acting Director in the Ministry of Public Works, granted golden-purple robes, and made him deputy commissioner of the metropolitan training command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian and again appointed Peng acting director in the Ministry of Public Works with golden-purple robes as deputy training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 頃之，攝江州刺史，州人便之。

translations.literal: Shortly after he acted as prefect of Jiangzhou; the people of the prefecture found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as acting prefect of Jiang, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，免喪，永平軍節度李勉署奏檢校工部郎中、兼侍御史，為判官，尋攝陳州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended, Li Mian, military governor of the Yongping army, appointed and memorialized him as Acting Director in the Ministry of Works and concurrent Attendant Censor as administrative aide; soon he acted as prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he rejoined Li Mian of Yongping as acting director in the Ministry of Works and attendant censor, then served as acting prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 歲中，即值李靈曜反於汴州，勉署芃兼亳州防禦使，練達軍事，兵備甚肅；

translations.literal: Within the year Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou. Mian appointed Peng concurrently defense commissioner of Bozhou; he was practiced in military affairs and his armaments were very strict;
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Lingyao rebelled at Bian. Mian made Peng concurrent defense commissioner of Bo; Peng was skilled in military affairs and kept the army in strict readiness;

sentences.zh: 又開陳、潁運路，以通漕輓。

translations.literal: he also opened the transport route through Chen and Ying to connect grain transport by water.
translations.idiomatic: and opened the Chen-Ying transport route to restore grain shipments.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，授檢校太常少卿、兼御史中丞、河陽三城鎮遏使。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Peng was appointed Acting Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrent Vice Censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of the three Heyang cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded, Peng was made acting vice minister of imperial sacrifices, vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of the three Heyang cities.

sentences.zh: 撫勞備至，資廩善者，必先軍士。

translations.literal: He comforted and encouraged with utmost thoroughness; of supplies and granaries that were good, the soldiers always received first.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his men exhaustively and always gave the best supplies to the soldiers first.

sentences.zh: 間一年，為節度使路嗣恭之副，加檢校左庶子、河陽三城懷州節度觀察使，以東畿汜水等五縣隸焉。

translations.literal: After a year he became deputy to the military governor Lu Sigong, was given the additional posts of Acting Left Subordinate Heir Apparent and military governor and observation commissioner of the three Heyang cities and Huaizhou, with five counties including Sishui of the eastern capital circuit placed under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became deputy to Lu Sigong, was made acting left subordinate heir apparent and military governor of Heyang and Huai, with five eastern capital counties including Si added to his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 時河南北連大兵，詔益以神策、汝、陝之師。

translations.literal: At that time great armies were continuously engaged north and south of the Yellow River; an edict added Shence troops and forces from Ru and Shan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: With major campaigns north and south of the Yellow River, an edict reinforced him with Shence troops and forces from Ru and Shan.

sentences.zh: 芃進收新鄉、共城，遂圍衛州。

translations.literal: Peng advanced to recover Xinxiang and Gongcheng, then besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng advanced to recover Xinxiang and Gongcheng and besieged Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔與河東節度馬燧等諸軍破田悅於洹水，以功加檢校兵部尚書，累封開郡王，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered him with Ma Sui, military governor of Hedong, and the various armies to defeat Tian Yue at Huanshui. For this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Minister of War, was enfeoffed cumulatively as Prince of Kai commandery, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined Ma Sui of Hedong and other armies in defeating Tian Yue at Huanshui, was made acting Minister of War, enfeoffed as Prince of Kai, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進圍悅於魏州，將符璘以精騎五百夜降，芃耳開營以納之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Yue at Weizhou, the general Fu Lin came over by night with five hundred elite horsemen; Peng opened the camp at his ear to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Yue at Wei, he received general Fu Lin's night defection with five hundred elite horsemen and opened the camp to admit them.

sentences.zh: 明日，歸璘於招討使。

translations.literal: The next day he returned Lin to the campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Lin on to the campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上居奉天，斂軍還。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengtian, he gathered his army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Fengtian, he withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 興元初，檢校右僕射，無何，以疾固讓罷歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Right; before long, because of illness he firmly petitioned to resign and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xingyuan (784) he was made acting right vice director of the imperial secretariat; soon illness compelled him to petition firmly for retirement.

sentences.zh: 芃將請告，謂所親曰：「今年夏被蝗旱，人主厭兵革，然則天下城壘堅厚矣，戈鋋銛利矣，以力勝之，則有得失，其可盡乎！

translations.literal: When Peng was about to request leave, he said to those close to him: "This summer we suffered locusts and drought; the ruler is weary of war. Yet the realm's walls and ramparts are thick and strong, spears and blades sharp — to overcome by force alone brings gain and loss; can it be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: As Peng prepared to request retirement, he told his intimates: "This summer brought locusts and drought; the emperor is weary of war. Yet walls are strong and weapons sharp — victory by force alone cannot be final.

sentences.zh: 除弊之急，莫先德化，循而理之，斯易致耳。

translations.literal: The urgent task in removing harm is none before moral transformation; to follow and govern accordingly is easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent cure is moral governance; rule patiently and success comes easily.

sentences.zh: 方鎮之戴翼時主，宜先退讓，貪權持祿，吾所不取也。

translations.literal: Regional commanders who support the timely ruler should first yield and withdraw; to grasp power and hold salary — that I do not take.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders who support the throne should yield first; I will not cling to power and salary.

sentences.zh: 吾既疾病，豈能言而不踐乎！」

translations.literal: Now that I am ill, how can I speak and not act!
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am ill, how can I speak thus and not act on it!

sentences.zh: 乃手疏乞罷。

translations.literal: He then personally wrote a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a personal memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年卒，年六十四，廢朝一日，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he died at age sixty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 785 at sixty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李澄李澄，遼東襄平人，隋蒲山公寬之後也，居京兆。

translations.literal: Li Cheng — Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a descendant of Sui's Duke of Pushan, Kuan, and resided in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, descended from Sui's Duke of Pushan, Kuan, and lived in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 父鎬，清江太守，以澄贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Hao was prefect of Qingjiang; because of Cheng he was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao was prefect of Qingjiang; Cheng's honors posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 澄以武藝為偏將，累除試將作監，隸於江淮都統李峘。

translations.literal: Cheng, through martial arts, became a junior general, was repeatedly appointed provisional Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, and was attached to Li Chuan, overall commander of Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rose through martial skill to junior general and provisional director of imperial manufactories under Li Chuan, overall commander of Jianghuai.

sentences.zh: 建中初，以檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞隸於永平軍節度使李勉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he served as Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-chief under Li Mian, military governor of the Yongping army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he served as acting guest of the heir apparent and vice censor-in-chief under Li Mian of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 及勉移理汴州，乃奏澄為滑州刺史。

translations.literal: When Mian transferred administration to Bianzhou, he memorialized that Cheng be made prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian moved his headquarters to Bian, he recommended Cheng as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，李希烈陷汴州，勉奔歸行在，澄遂以城降希烈，偽署尚書令，兼滑州永平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Li Xilie took Bianzhou; Mian fled back to the imperial camp, and Cheng thereupon surrendered the city to Xilie, who falsely appointed him Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrent military governor of Huazhou and the Yongping army.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 783 Li Xilie took Bian; Mian fled to the emperor's camp and Cheng surrendered Hua to Xilie, who made him minister of the imperial secretariat and military governor of Hua and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 興元元年春，澄密令親信人盧融間道賚表達於奉天，上嘉之，乃以帛詔藏於蠟丸中，加澄刑部尚書，兼汴州刺史、汴滑節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng secretly sent his trusted man Lu Rong by a bypath to deliver a memorial reaching Fengtian. The emperor commended this and placed an edict written on silk inside a wax pellet, promoting Cheng to Minister of Justice, concurrent prefect of Bianzhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Bian and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 784 Cheng secretly sent his confidant Lu Rong by a hidden route with a memorial to Fengtian. The emperor commended him and sent an edict in a wax pellet, promoting him to Minister of Justice, prefect of Bian, and military governor of Bian and Hua.

sentences.zh: 澄秘而未宣，乃集州兵嚴加訓習。

translations.literal: Cheng kept it secret and did not announce it; he then gathered the prefectural troops and trained them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng kept the edict secret and mustered the prefectural troops for strict training.

sentences.zh: 希烈頗疑之，乃令養子六百人戍之，以虞其變。

translations.literal: Xilie was quite suspicious and therefore stationed six hundred adopted sons to garrison it, to guard against any change.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie grew suspicious and stationed six hundred adopted sons as a garrison to watch him.

sentences.zh: 希烈苦攻寧陵，邀澄率其眾至石柱。

translations.literal: Xilie pressed hard in attacking Ningling and summoned Cheng to lead his host to Shizhu.
translations.idiomatic: While Xilie besieged Ningling he summoned Cheng and his troops to Shizhu.

sentences.zh: 澄令縱火焚營，而偽遁，誘六百人因驚行剽而加其罪，果大俘掠，悉令斬之以告。

translations.literal: Cheng ordered fires set to burn the camp while feigning flight, luring the six hundred men to panic, march out plundering, and thereby incur guilt; they indeed looted on a great scale, and he had them all beheaded and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng set fire to the camp and feigned flight, provoking the six hundred into panic looting; he then had them all executed and reported their crimes to Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈不能窮詰焉。

translations.literal: Xilie could not investigate to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie could not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 無凡，希烈遣其將翟暉等寇陳州，久之未復。

translations.literal: Before long Xilie sent his generals Zhai Hui and others to raid Chenzhou; for a long time they did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xilie sent generals including Zhai Hui against Chen, and they were long absent.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，澄以汴州兵寡，度希烈不能制己，又會中官薛盈珍持節且至，加檢校兵部尚書，封武威郡王，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Cheng judged that Bianzhou's troops were few and estimated that Xilie could not control him; moreover the palace eunuch Xue Yingzhen was coming with credentials, and he was promoted to Acting Minister of War, enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei commandery, and granted a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That October Cheng judged Bian's forces too few for Xilie to control him, learned that eunuch Xue Yingzhen was arriving with credentials, and received promotion to acting Minister of War, enfeoffment as Prince of Wuwei, and a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 澄乃乘勢力焚賊旌節，誓眾歸國。

translations.literal: Cheng then seized the momentum, burned the rebel banners and credentials, and swore the host to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng seized the moment, burned the rebel banners and credentials, and swore his troops back to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及十一月，希烈既失澄，又聞翟暉大敗，由是奔歸蔡州。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month Xilie had lost Cheng and also heard that Zhai Hui had suffered a great defeat; for this reason he fled back to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By November Xilie had lost Cheng and heard of Zhai Hui's crushing defeat; he fled back to Cai.

sentences.zh: 澄遽率眾將復汴州，屯於城北門，恇怯不敢進。

translations.literal: Cheng hastily led his host intending to recover Bianzhou, encamped at the north gate of the city, but in timidity and fear did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng hurried to recover Bian and camped at the north gate, but fear held him back from entering.

sentences.zh: 及宣武軍節度使劉洽師至城東門，賊將田懷珍開關以納之。

translations.literal: When Liu Qia, military governor of the Xuanwu army, reached the army to the east gate of the city, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the pass to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qia of Xuanwu reached the east gate, rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the gates to admit him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，澄方自北入，洽已據子城。

translations.literal: The next day Cheng only then entered from the north; Qia had already occupied the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cheng entered from the north only to find Qia already holding the inner city.

sentences.zh: 澄乃舍於浚儀縣，兩軍將士，日有忿競，不自安。

translations.literal: Cheng then lodged in Junyi county; the officers and soldiers of the two armies daily had angry quarrels and were ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng withdrew to Junyi county; the two armies quarreled daily and lived in mutual unease.

sentences.zh: 會鄭州賊將孫液通款於澄，澄遣其子清赴之。

translations.literal: It happened that Sun Ye, a rebel general of Zhengzhou, opened negotiations with Cheng; Cheng sent his son Qing to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Sun Ye of Zheng offered terms to Cheng, who sent his son Qing to accept.

sentences.zh: 先是，河陽軍節度使李芃遣其將雍顥攻鄭州，顥所過縱掠，液拒之尤固；

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Peng, military governor of the Heyang army, had sent his general Yong Hao to attack Zhengzhou; wherever Hao passed he allowed looting, and Ye resisted him especially firmly;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Peng of Heyang had sent general Yong Hao against Zheng; Hao plundered along the way and Ye resisted him fiercely;

sentences.zh: 及清至，遂納之。

translations.literal: when Qing arrived, Ye thereupon submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: when Qing arrived, Ye submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 顥怒攻液，清以眾助之，殺登城者數十人，顥方引退，又焚陽武而歸。

translations.literal: Hao angrily attacked Ye; Qing aided him with his host, killing several dozen men on the walls; Hao only then withdrew, and again burned Yangwu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hao attacked in fury; Qing reinforced Ye and killed dozens on the walls. Hao withdrew, burning Yangwu as he went.

sentences.zh: 澄乃出赴鄭州，朝廷特授清檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞，更名克寧。

translations.literal: Cheng then went out to Zhengzhou; the court specially appointed Qing Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-chief, and changed his name to Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng went to Zheng in person; the court specially appointed Qing acting guest of the heir apparent and vice censor-in-chief, renaming him Kening.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年三月，就加澄檢校左僕射、義成軍鄭滑許等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhenyuan, Cheng was thereupon given the additional posts of Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Left and military governor of the Yicheng army and the prefectures Zheng, Hua, Xu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 785 Cheng was made acting left vice director of the imperial secretariat and military governor of the Yicheng army and Zheng, Hua, Xu, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年五十四，廢朝一日，贈司空，賵布帛粟有差，仍令左散騎常侍歸崇敬充弔祭使，所緣喪葬，並勒官給。

translations.literal: In the second year he died at age fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously given Minister of Works. Funeral gifts of cloth, silk, and grain were given in graded amounts, and the Left Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat Gui Jingchong was ordered to serve as mourning envoy; all funeral expenses along the route were commanded to be supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 786 at fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain. Gui Jingchong, left regular attendant, was sent as mourning envoy, and all funeral costs were paid by the state.

sentences.zh: 澄實以八月癸未終，克寧秘之，以九月庚寅，欲自起視事。

translations.literal: Cheng in fact died on the day guiwei in the eighth month; Kening concealed it, and on the day gengyin in the ninth month wished to rise himself and attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had actually died on guiwei day in the eighth month; Kening concealed the death and on gengyin day in the ninth month tried to take command himself.

sentences.zh: 其行軍司馬馬鉉不許，克寧陰遣殺之，乃墨絰而出，加卒於城門，將為不順。

translations.literal: His campaigning army marshal Ma Xuan would not permit it; Kening secretly sent men to kill him, then came out wearing black mourning headcloth, added guards at the city gates, and was about to act in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His army marshal Ma Xuan refused; Kening had him killed secretly, donned mourning garb, posted extra guards at the gates, and prepared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 劉洽出師屯於境上以制之，且使告諭切至，由是克寧不敢妄發，然道路絕商旅者凡十四五日。

translations.literal: Liu Qia led troops out and encamped on the border to restrain him, and also sent envoys with stern admonitions; thereby Kening did not dare act rashly, yet travelers and merchants were cut off from the roads for fourteen or fifteen days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia marched to the border to restrain him and sent stern warnings; Kening dared not move, but travel was cut off for fourteen or fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 及賈躭代澄，克寧護喪將歸，乃悉索府中財貨，以夜出城，軍人從而剽奪，及明殆盡。

translations.literal: When Jia Dan replaced Cheng, Kening escorted the coffin homeward and then seized all wealth and goods in the headquarters, leaving the city by night; soldiers followed in plundering, and by dawn nearly everything was gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Dan succeeded Cheng, Kening escorted the coffin home, looted the headquarters by night, and soldiers joined the plunder until nearly everything was gone by dawn.

sentences.zh: 澄柩至京師，又賜克寧莊一所、錢千貫、粟麥二千石。

translations.literal: When Cheng's coffin reached the capital, Kening was again granted one estate, one thousand strings of cash, and two thousand piculs of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng's coffin reached the capital, Kening was granted an estate, one thousand strings of cash, and two thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 澄初封隴西郡公，進武威郡王，每上疏連稱二封，頗為時人所哂。

translations.literal: Cheng was first enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery, then advanced to Prince of Wuwei commandery; in every memorial he linked both titles together, and was quite ridiculed by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was first enfeoffed Duke of Longxi, then Prince of Wuwei; he cited both titles in every memorial and was widely mocked for it.

sentences.zh: 李元素李元素，字大朴，蒲山公密之孫。

translations.literal: Li Yuansu — Li Yuansu, courtesy name Dapu, was a grandson of Duke of Pushan, Mi.
