translations.idiomatic: Li Yuansu, courtesy name Dapu, was a grandson of Duke of Pushan, Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 任侍御史，時杜亞為東都留守，惡大將令狐運，會盜發洛城之北，運適與其部下畋於北郊，亞意其為盜，遂執訊之，逮系者四十餘人。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Censor. At that time Du Ya was eastern capital regent and hated the great general Linghu Yun. It happened that robbers struck north of Luoyang; Yun happened to be hunting in the northern suburbs with his subordinates. Ya suspected him of being the robber, seized and interrogated him, and more than forty persons were arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant censor. Du Ya, regent of the eastern capital, hated general Linghu Yun. When robbers struck north of Luoyang, Yun happened to be hunting in the northern suburbs with his men. Ya arrested him as the culprit and imprisoned more than forty people.

sentences.zh: 監察御史楊寧按其事，亞以為不直，密表陳之，寧遂得罪。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Yang Ning investigated the case; Ya considered him unjust and secretly memorialized against him; Ning thereupon was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Yang Ning reviewed the case; Ya considered him biased, secretly denounced him, and Yang was punished.

sentences.zh: 亞將逞其宿怒，且以得賊為功，上表指明運為盜之狀，上信而不疑。

translations.literal: Ya was about to vent his old anger and also take catching the robbers as merit; he memorialized specifying Yun's conduct as that of the robber. The emperor believed and did not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Ya meant to vent old grudges and claim credit for catching the robbers; he memorialized identifying Yun as the culprit, and the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以獄大宜審，奏請覆之，命元素就決，亞迎路以獄成告。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, because the case was great and ought to be carefully examined, memorialized requesting a review and ordered Yuansu to go decide it. Ya met him on the road and announced that the case was already concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, finding the case too grave to rush, asked for review and sent Yuansu to decide. Ya met him on the road and declared the case closed.

sentences.zh: 元素驗之五日，盡釋其囚以還。

translations.literal: Yuansu examined it for five days and released all the prisoners to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu investigated for five days and released every prisoner.

sentences.zh: 亞大驚，且怒，親追送，馬上責之，元素不答。

translations.literal: Ya was greatly startled and also angry; he personally pursued and saw him off, rebuking him from horseback. Yuansu did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was shocked and furious; he rode after Yuansu and rebuked him from horseback. Yuansu did not answer.

sentences.zh: 亞遂上疏，又誣元素。

translations.literal: Ya then submitted a memorial again slandering Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Ya then memorialized again, slandering Yuansu.

sentences.zh: 元素還奏，言未畢，上怒曰：「出俟命。」

translations.literal: Yuansu returned to report; before he had finished speaking the emperor angrily said, "Go out and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu reported to court; before he finished the emperor snapped, "Leave and await orders.

sentences.zh: 元素曰：「臣未盡詞。」

translations.literal: Yuansu said, "Your servant has not finished his words."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu said, "I have not finished speaking."

sentences.zh: 上又曰：「且去」。

translations.literal: The emperor again said, "Go for now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said again, "Go now."

sentences.zh: 元素復奏曰：「一出不得復見陛下，乞容盡詞。」

translations.literal: Yuansu again reported: "Once I go out I cannot again see Your Majesty; I beg permission to finish my words.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu persisted: "If I leave now I may never see Your Majesty again — let me finish.

sentences.zh: 上意稍緩，元素盡言運冤狀明白，上乃寤曰：「非卿，孰能辨之！」

translations.literal: The emperor's mood gradually eased. Yuansu fully stated Yun's wrongful suffering clearly. The emperor then awoke and said, "Without you, sir, who could have distinguished this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented. Yuansu laid out Yun's innocence clearly, and the emperor exclaimed, "Without you, who could have seen this!"

sentences.zh: 後數月，竟得其真賊，元素由是為時器重，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Several months later they finally obtained the true robbers. Yuansu thereby came to be highly valued by his contemporaries and was transferred to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the real robbers were caught. Yuansu won wide respect and was made drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 時美官缺，必指元素。

translations.literal: Whenever a fine office was vacant, Yuansu was always the one named.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prestigious post opened, Yuansu was the name put forward.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant minister of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 數月，鄭滑節度盧群卒，遂命元素兼御史大夫，鎮鄭滑，就加檢校工部尚書，在鎮稱理。

translations.literal: Several months later Lu Qun, military governor of Zheng-Hua, died; Yuansu was then ordered to serve concurrently as Censor-in-chief, garrison Zheng-Hua, and was thereupon given the additional post of Acting Minister of Works. In his command he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Lu Qun of Zheng-Hua died; Yuansu was made concurrent censor-in-chief and governor of Zheng-Hua with acting Minister of Works, and governed well.

sentences.zh: 元和初，征拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was summoned to court as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 自貞元中位缺，久難其人，至是元素以名望召拜，中外聳聽。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era the post had been vacant and for long the right man was hard to find; now Yuansu was summoned and appointed for his renown, and court and countryside listened with awe.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been vacant since Zhenyuan and long lacked a worthy holder; Yuansu's appointment by reputation stirred court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 及居位，一無修舉，但規求作相。

translations.literal: When he took the post he made not a single improvement or achievement, but only plotted to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In office he accomplished nothing but schemed for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 久之，浸不得志，見客必曰：「無以某官散相疏也。」

translations.literal: After a long while he gradually failed to achieve his aims; whenever he saw guests he always said, "Do not treat me, an official of such rank, with the distance of a mere associate councilor.
translations.idiomatic: As hopes faded he told every visitor, "Do not treat me like some minor councilor.

sentences.zh: 見屬官必先拜，脂韋在列，大失人情。

translations.literal: When he saw subordinate officials he always bowed first; fawning and servile men filled the ranks, and he greatly lost popular regard.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed first to his own subordinates; sycophants filled his staff, and he lost all goodwill.

sentences.zh: 李錡為亂江南，遂授元素浙西道節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: When Li Qi rebelled in Jiangnan, Yuansu was then appointed military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of the Zhexi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi rebelled in the lower Yangzi, Yuansu was made military governor and disposition commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 數月受代，入拜國子祭酒，尋遷太常卿，轉戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: After several months he was replaced; he entered court as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, soon was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then became Minister of Revenue and administrator of the Commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was replaced, became chancellor of the directorate of education, then minister of imperial sacrifices, then minister of revenue and commissariat administrator.

sentences.zh: 元素少孤，奉長姊友敬加於人，及其姊歿，沉悲遘疾，上疏懇辭，從之。

translations.literal: Yuansu was orphaned young and served his elder sister with friendship and respect beyond ordinary people; when his sister died he sank into grief and fell ill, submitted a earnest memorial requesting leave, and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yuansu honored his elder sister devotedly; when she died he fell into grief and illness and petitioned earnestly for leave, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 數月，以出妻免官。

translations.literal: Several months later he was dismissed from office for divorcing his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was dismissed for divorcing his wife.

sentences.zh: 初，元素再娶妻王氏，石泉公方慶之孫，性柔弱，元素為郎官時娶之，甚禮重，及貴，溺情僕妾，遂薄之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuansu had taken a second wife, the Wang clan, granddaughter of Duke of Shiquan, Fang Qing; her nature was gentle and yielding. When Yuansu was a bureau official he married her and treated her with great ceremonial respect; when he became eminent he doted on servant-girls and concubines and therefore slighted her.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu had remarried Lady Wang, granddaughter of Fang Qing, Duke of Shiquan — a gentle woman he had married as a young official and treated with respect until rank and concubines made him neglect her.

sentences.zh: 且又無子，而前妻之子已長，無良，元素寢疾昏惑，聽譖遂出之，給與非厚。

translations.literal: Moreover she had no son, while the son of his former wife had grown up and was worthless. Yuansu, lying ill and confused, listened to slanders and thereupon divorced her, with provision not generous.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no children; his grown son by a former wife was worthless. Ill and confused, Yuansu heeded slander, divorced her, and gave her a meager settlement.

sentences.zh: 妻族上訴，乃詔曰：「李元素病中上表，懇切披陳，雲『妻王氏，禮義殊乖，願與離絕』。

translations.literal: Her clan appealed upward, and an edict said: "Li Yuansu, while ill, submitted a memorial earnestly laying bare his case, saying, 'My wife the Wang clan is utterly at odds with ritual and righteousness; I wish to separate from her.
translations.idiomatic: Her family appealed to the throne, and an edict declared: "Li Yuansu, while ill, petitioned earnestly that his wife Lady Wang had violated ritual and he wished to divorce her.

sentences.zh: 初謂素有醜行，不能顯言，以其大官之家，所以令自處置。

translations.literal: At first it was thought she had long had shameful conduct that could not be stated openly; because hers was a great official family, he was therefore allowed to handle it himself.
translations.idiomatic: We assumed longstanding misconduct he could not state openly and, given her eminent family, allowed him to act on his own.

sentences.zh: 訪聞不曾告報妻族，亦無明過可書，蓋是中情不和，遂至於此。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was learned that he had never informed her clan, nor was there any clear fault that could be recorded — it was simply that their inner feelings were not in harmony, and so it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed he never informed her family and no clear fault could be found — only mutual incompatibility.

sentences.zh: 脅以王命，當日遣歸，給送之間，又至單薄。

translations.literal: Coerced by imperial command, she was sent home that same day; in the provisions for her departure they were again exceedingly meager.
translations.idiomatic: Compelled by imperial order she was sent home the same day with a settlement far too meager.

sentences.zh: 不唯王氏受辱，實亦朝情悉驚。

translations.literal: Not only did the Wang clan suffer humiliation — in truth court sentiment was entirely shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was humiliated and the court was shocked.

sentences.zh: 如此理家，合當懲責。

translations.literal: To manage a household in this way deserved punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct in managing his household deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 宜停官，仍令與王氏錢物，通所奏數滿五千貫。」

translations.literal: He should be removed from office, and was still ordered to give the Wang clan money and goods totaling the five thousand strings he had reported in his memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: He is dismissed from office and ordered to pay Lady Wang five thousand strings in all, as he himself had proposed."

sentences.zh: 元和五年卒，贈陝州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously given Grand Protector of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 810 and was posthumously made grand protector of Shan.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：李抱玉、李抱真，以武勇之材，兼忠義之行，有唐之良將也。

translations.literal: [Appraisal] The historiographer says: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen, with martial valor as their material and loyal righteousness as their conduct, were fine generals of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: [Appraisal] The historiographer writes: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen combined martial courage with loyal conduct — true Tang generals.

sentences.zh: 且如農隙教潞人之射，數騎入武俊之營，非有奇謀，孰能如是。

translations.literal: Consider teaching the people of Lu to shoot in the intervals of farming, or entering Wujun's camp with only a few horsemen — without extraordinary stratagem, who could do such things?
translations.idiomatic: Training Lu peasants to shoot in farming seasons, riding into Wang Wujun's camp with a handful of men — without exceptional daring, who could do such things?

sentences.zh: 惜乎服食求仙，為藥所誤。

translations.literal: Alas that in ingesting elixirs and seeking transcendence he was misled by drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Alas that he swallowed elixirs seeking immortality and was destroyed by them.

sentences.zh: 王虔休不黨僭命，有足可嘉；

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu did not join the usurpers' faction — there is much to commend;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu refused the usurpers' cause and deserves praise;

sentences.zh: 盧從史動多懷奸，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi in his actions harbored much treachery and brought calamity on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi's treachery brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 芃則老也知足，澄則過而改圖。

translations.literal: Peng in old age knew contentment; Cheng, having erred, changed his course.
translations.idiomatic: Peng in age knew when to be content; Cheng, having erred, changed course.

sentences.zh: 元素為御史時，執德不回；

translations.literal: When Yuansu was a censor he held to virtue without turning aside;
translations.idiomatic: As censor Yuansu held firm to principle;

sentences.zh: 居大夫日，其心甚短。

translations.literal: in the days when he was Censor-in-chief, his heart was very small.
translations.idiomatic: as censor-in-chief his spirit proved small.

sentences.zh: 因緣七出，益露醜聲，善少惡多，又何足算。

translations.literal: Using the seven grounds for divorce as pretext, he further exposed his shameful reputation — little good and much evil; what is there to reckon?
translations.idiomatic: His divorce on flimsy grounds exposed his shame — virtues few, faults many; little worth counting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：抱玉、抱真，我朝良將。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Baoyu and Baozhen — fine generals of our court.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Baoyu and Baozhen — our court's fine generals.

sentences.zh: 虔休之心，亦多可尚。

translations.literal: Qianxiu's heart, too, has much to admire.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu's loyalty, too, deserves respect.

sentences.zh: 史懷奸謀，芃將祿讓。

translations.literal: Congshi harbored treacherous plots; Peng was about to yield salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi plotted treachery; Peng yielded rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 澄迷卻行，素貪一響。

translations.literal: Cheng, lost, turned back his march; Yuansu, greedy, sought one echo of fame.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng turned from error; Yuansu grasped for a single note of fame.

sentences.zh: 吾誰與欺，豈如忠諒。

translations.literal: Whom would I deceive? How could it compare to loyal sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Whom would I deceive? Loyal sincerity is the measure.
